findings: Partial-receive workflow gap (possible): canBeDelivered() allows receiving against POs with status RECEIVED, enabling multiple partial deliveries. Verify that warehouse staff understand a RECEIVED PO can still be re-received for partial shipments, and that the UI clearly distinguishes "partially received" from "fully completed."

Lock scope in convertRequestToPurchaseOrder (confirmed): The row lock is on the procurement_requests table row, preventing duplicate conversion of the same request. It does not prevent two different approved requests for the same product from being converted to separate POs concurrently. If the intent is to prevent duplicate POs per product-supplier pair, the lock or uniqueness check should be at the PO or product level, not the request level.

deliverPurchaseOrder hard failure (confirmed): The deprecated method throws BadMethodCallException immediately. Any code path that still calls this method will break. Verify no other controllers, services, or background jobs reference deliverPurchaseOrder.

Frontend receive button shows for RECEIVED status (confirmed): The button visibility condition enables partial re-receives. Ensure the modal or receive form indicates remaining quantity and cumulative received quantity per item, so warehouse staff don't accidentally double-receive.
